text:
🦉 Immunology Patent Signals

October 1–31, 2026 | Monthly Immunology Patent Digest | UTC

October's patent disclosures reveal a shift in how researchers are trying to improve immunotherapy.

More powerful immune activation is no longer the only objective. Several inventions seek to control where T cells activate, separate expansion from tumor recognition, overcome vascular and metabolic barriers, or identify toxicity before treatment begins.

We selected 12 patent developments that illustrate these approaches. Some contain intriguing experimental evidence. Others remain technical proposals with substantial questions unanswered.

The most interesting theme is how differently developers are addressing the same problem: making immune cells effective without making them dangerously indiscriminate.

📜 1. When Removing a Signal Might Improve CAR-T Function

CAR designs usually add signaling domains to increase T-cell activation. An October patent takes an unexpectedly different direction.

Vanudis describes an accessory immune-cell recruiting receptor that uses the transmembrane region of an adhesion molecule, while weakening or completely removing its intracellular costimulatory signaling domain.

The document describes experimental findings that challenge the assumption that additional intracellular signaling is always necessary for improved antigen sensitivity.

The scientific question is important: can receptor architecture and membrane organization improve immune-cell function without simply adding more activating signals?

That would offer a different route to improving engineered T cells. But evidence from patent examples is not equivalent to independent clinical validation, and the precise contribution of membrane geometry versus other receptor properties still requires investigation.

Vanudis · WO2026209887A1 · October 8 · International patent application
https://t.co/Y40mHSuVI8

📜 2. T-Cell Engagers That Respond to Tumor Acidity

A bispecific antibody can recognize a tumor antigen and recruit a T cell. The difficulty is that tumor-associated antigens are rarely exclusive to cancer.

BigHat Biosciences proposes another layer of selectivity: CEACAM6×CD3 T-cell engagers engineered to bind more strongly in acidic conditions.

In one disclosed binding example, CD3 affinity improved approximately tenfold, from around 200 nM at pH 7.4 to 20 nM at pH 6.0. The platform also explores low-affinity, high-avidity CEACAM6 recognition.

Rather than relying entirely on antigen expression, the design attempts to exploit a property of the tumor environment.

The distinction matters. Acid-sensitive binding could help discriminate between tissues, but it does not automatically establish tumor-specific killing or a favorable therapeutic window. Normal tissues can also experience acidic conditions, and clinical safety has not been demonstrated.

BigHat Biosciences · WO2026222338A1 · October 22 · International patent application
https://t.co/l9zIuYyfZG

📜 3. Expanding CAR-T Cells Without Their Tumor Antigen

One of October's most interesting inventions separates CAR-T expansion from direct recognition of the tumor.

Innovative Cellular Therapeutics describes a system containing three populations: PAP-targeted CAR-T cells, CD19-targeted CAR-T cells, and CD19-positive B cells.

The CD19 CAR-T/B-cell interaction provides costimulatory and cytokine signals that support expansion of the PAP-targeted cells, even without engagement of their own tumor antigen.

In the patent's mouse experiments, circulating PAP CAR-T cells expanded more than fivefold relative to PAP CAR-T treatment alone at day 14. The combined system also improved tumor control in a prostate cancer xenograft model.

This challenges an important assumption about adoptive cell therapy: that therapeutic T cells must repeatedly encounter their target antigen to expand effectively.

But the three-component system adds manufacturing and dosing complexity. Its apparent advantages in memory-associated phenotypes and exhaustion markers still need clinical testing.

Innovative Cellular Therapeutics · US20260325581A1 · October 22 · Published US application
https://t.co/l9FHdmkdrM

📜 4. Engineering CAR-T Cells Inside the Patient

Stanford University proposes a targeted lentiviral platform designed to deliver CAR constructs directly to T cells.

The vector carries a modified VSV-G protein that does not bind the conventional LDL receptor, alongside T-cell-targeting binding fragments. It also encodes both a CAR and an IL-9 receptor.

The goal is to make gene delivery more selective and potentially generate therapeutic CAR-T cells in vivo rather than relying exclusively on centralized ex vivo manufacturing.

There is an important technical obstacle here. A gene-delivery system must reach the intended cells, avoid unwanted transduction, achieve adequate expression, and remain safe.

The patent describes a proposed solution to these problems; it does not establish that in vivo manufacturing is clinically equivalent to conventional CAR-T production.

Stanford University · WO2026226990A1 · October 29 · International patent application
https://t.co/CaE60Vjujd

📜 5. CAR-T Cells That Also Target the Tumor's Blood Supply

Destroying cancer cells is not the only challenge in solid tumors. Their abnormal vasculature can limit immune-cell access and reinforce an immunosuppressive microenvironment.

A patent from Massachusetts General Hospital describes CAR-T cells that also express a bispecific antibody targeting VEGF and angiopoietin-2.

The concept combines tumor-antigen recognition with local interference in two pathways involved in vascular remodeling.

This is a different kind of CAR-T armoring. Rather than giving the cells another cytotoxic receptor, the design aims to change conditions around the tumor.

Whether simultaneous VEGF/Ang2 blockade improves trafficking, efficacy, or safety compared with established approaches remains an experimental question. The patent itself cannot establish a clinical advantage.

The General Hospital Corporation · WO2026226941A1 · October 29 · International patent application
https://t.co/1djuqzngH7

📜 6. Two Receptor Signals, Two Opposing CAR-T Outcomes

Not all immune receptors contribute equally to CAR-T persistence.

Kite Pharma's October application describes engineering TIGIT and CD27 pathways to improve cell function.

The document includes analyses of CAR-T products and clinical outcomes from subsets of the ZUMA-1, ZUMA-6, and ZUMA-7 studies. Higher CD27-related signaling features were associated with durable responses, whereas TIGIT-associated interactions were linked to progression.

The proposed engineering strategies include reducing TIGIT expression, introducing switch receptors, strengthening CD27 signaling, and selecting particular T-cell populations during manufacturing.

The interesting idea is that CAR-T performance may depend as much on the balance of inhibitory and supportive signals as on antigen recognition.

Yet associations in patient samples do not establish that engineering these pathways will improve survival. That requires prospective intervention studies.

Kite Pharma · WO2026226640A1 · October 29 · International patent application
https://t.co/qFQoB2zjFX

📜 7. Can CAR-T Neurotoxicity Be Predicted Before Infusion?

Most CAR-T safety assessments focus on patient characteristics, treatment exposures, and clinical changes after infusion.

Seattle Children's proposes looking directly at protein-interaction networks within the therapeutic cells.

Its patent describes biosignatures intended to distinguish cell products associated with neurotoxicity or cytokine release syndrome, potentially informing prediction or preventive intervention.

The idea is appealing because conventional cytotoxicity assays may miss cellular features that contribute to toxicity in patients.

The central unanswered question is predictive performance. Without independent prospective validation, a molecular signature cannot be assumed to reliably identify which patients will develop ICANS or severe CRS.

Seattle Children's Research Institute · WO2026218003A2 · October 15 · International patent application; accessible abstract
https://t.co/3qqvMTdo4w

📜 8. When Immunotherapy Becomes an Alternative to Surgery

An October application from Memorial Sloan Kettering covers methods of treating selected nonmetastatic mismatch-repair-deficient solid tumors without surgery.

The disclosed approaches include PD-1 blockade alone or combined with CTLA-4 inhibition, with clinical complete response forming part of the claimed treatment strategy.

The important development is not the discovery of PD-1 inhibition. It is the attempt to define and protect specific organ-preserving treatment methods.

This raises questions about patient selection, duration of response, surveillance, and the evidence needed before surgery can safely be omitted.

A patent application does not answer those clinical questions. Nor does publication of the claims represent regulatory authorization for a particular nonsurgical treatment strategy.

Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center · WO2026226924A2 · October 29 · International patent application
https://t.co/x9e7vO4Be7

📜 9. Selecting Patients for Dual PD-1/VEGF-Pathway Inhibition

Blocking PD-1 and VEGF-related signaling can alter both immune suppression and the tumor microenvironment. But benefit varies considerably between cancer types and patients.

Summit Therapeutics' October application describes baseline tumor biomarkers for selecting or guiding treatment involving PD-1 inhibition alongside VEGFR-pathway inhibition.

The potential value is straightforward: a combination therapy becomes more useful if clinicians can identify the patients most likely to benefit.

The difficult part is proving that a marker is predictive rather than merely prognostic. Clinical use would require defined assays, reproducible thresholds, and validation showing that marker-guided treatment improves decisions.

Summit Therapeutics · WO2026208876A1 · October 8 · International patent application
https://t.co/KRCNNbvZjx

📜 10. Borrowing Antimicrobial Immunity to Attack Tumors

What happens if cancer immunotherapy recruits an immune response normally directed against infection?

IMMREJ describes therapeutic approaches that introduce or exploit microbial antigenic features to generate an anti-infection-like T-cell response within tumors or metastatic sites.

The proposed strategy combines this response with other cancer immunotherapies.

Its appeal is that an existing or inducible antimicrobial immune response might be redirected toward cancer. Its weakness is equally important: efficient immune priming does not guarantee selective tumor killing, durable control, or acceptable inflammation.

The accessible disclosure establishes the proposed method, not clinical proof of synergy.

IMMREJ · WO2026218097A1 · October 22 · International patent application
https://t.co/ajIRPoYKf7

📜 11. Making Cancer Vaccines More Immunogenic Without More Reactogenicity

Immune stimulation presents a familiar problem in vaccine engineering: the same delivery system that activates useful immunity may also cause unwanted inflammation.

HDT Bio's October disclosure describes nanoparticles carrying nucleic acids and regulatory elements, including microRNA-binding sites, intended to influence reactogenicity and promote innate and adaptive immune responses.

Potential applications include therapeutic vaccines against cancer.

The technical idea is to engineer the delivery platform and its biological regulation together, rather than treating delivery as a passive transport problem.

The decisive tests will be whether reduced reactogenicity is accompanied by sufficient antigen-specific immunity, reproducible delivery, and clinically relevant antitumor activity.

HDT Bio · WO2026221982A2 · October 22 · International patent application; accessible abstract
https://t.co/c19hiBaKrp

📜 12. Dual-Target CARs: A Patent Grant, Not a New Discovery

October also brought an actual US patent grant covering a bispecific CAR directed against CD20 and BCMA.

AbelZeta's patent defines particular antigen-binding regions, their sequences, and their arrangement within the receptor. The disclosed applications include cancer and autoimmune disease.

Its significance is different from the preceding applications. This is a legal-status development: the US patent was granted on October 6, after an earlier application publication in May 2025.

The distinction is worth emphasizing. A granted patent protects specific allowed claims; it does not prove clinical efficacy or establish exclusive control over every possible CD20/BCMA combination.

AbelZeta · US12751973B2 · October 6 · Granted US patent; earlier public disclosure
https://t.co/OSyxXPyy6U

💡What These Patents Tell Us About the Direction of Immunotherapy

Three broader conclusions emerge from this selection.

First, control is becoming as important as potency.

The Vanudis, BigHat, Kite, and Seattle Children's disclosures approach immune activation from different directions: receptor architecture, environmental selectivity, intracellular signaling, and toxicity prediction. Their common objective is to improve useful activity without unnecessarily increasing harmful activity.

They are not interchangeable technologies, and their evidence comes from different experimental settings. But together they expose a limitation of simply pursuing stronger immune stimulation.

Second, the boundary between the therapeutic cell and its environment is becoming less rigid.

The Massachusetts General Hospital platform couples CAR recognition with vascular targeting. Stanford proposes targeted gene delivery directly to T cells. The CoupledCAR system uses additional immune-cell populations to support expansion without the tumor antigen.

These approaches differ fundamentally in complexity. One modifies the tumor environment, another changes where cell engineering happens, and a third changes how therapeutic cells receive growth signals.

None can yet be declared superior. Each solves one problem while introducing others involving specificity, manufacturability, control, or safety.

Third, patent disclosures are advancing across several levels of evidence — and those levels must not be confused.

Some documents contain comparative binding experiments, cellular assays, or animal-model results. Others primarily define proposed treatment methods or biomarker strategies. A patent grant adds legal certainty to particular claims, not biological validation.

For the field, the key distinction is between an invention that can be described, a mechanism that can be demonstrated, and a treatment that improves patient outcomes.

October's disclosures offer numerous ideas worth testing. The next decisive advances will come from determining which of those ideas survive rigorous comparative experiments and, eventually, clinical trials.

Etymology & Origin
Latin Root: Patricius is derived from pater, the Latin word for "father." In ancient Rome, the patricii (patricians) were members of the original ruling aristocratic class.
Christian Popularization: The name spread widely because of the 5th-century Saint Patrick, the Romanized Briton born Sucat who was captured by Irish raiders, escaped, and later returned as a bishop to Christianize Ireland.
Irish Forms: In Irish Gaelic, the name is rendered as Pádraig (or older forms like Patraicc). Historically, it was rarely used as an everyday given name in Ireland for centuries because it was considered too sacred to honor the saint lightly, though it became common after the 17th century.

The word "patrack" (more accurately spelled patîkr or patikar in ancient Middle-Eastern contexts) does not have a Babylonian origin, but is instead an Old Iranian word meaning "sculpture" or "image" that entered Jewish Babylonian Aramaic and Biblical Aramaic via cultural and linguistic contact.
Linguistic Evolution
Proto-Iranian root: Derived from patikárah, meaning a likeness, model, or sculpted image.
Aramaic adoption: Passed into Biblical Aramaic as פתכר (ptkr, meaning sculpture or idol) and Jewish Babylonian Aramaic as פתיכרי (ptkrʾ / pṯaḵrā).

About The Site:
Needless to say, St. Peter's Square (Piazza San Pietro) is the large circular plaza located in front of St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican City. Current St. Peter's Square was designed by Giovanni Lorenzo Bernini, and completed in 1667, have a width of 200 meters, depth is 165 meters, surrounded by the columns of the corridor. We can see the panoramic landscape of the square from the top of Basilica, which was designed by Michelangelo Buonarroti. It's worth to toil up to the Cupola (Dome). Although we can use the elevator until the middle way, but it's always crowded, and we must climb the narrow staircase of 320 steps after getting off the elevator. So, I walked up to the top without using the elevator.

How To Get There:
The entrance of Vatican City is about 400 meters south of Ottaviano Station on Metro Line "A". We wouldn't lose the way because many people are walking toward the Vatican City. Among them, some people are heading to the ticket office of Vatican Museum. In such a case, we should proceed in the opposite direction of the line along with the wall of Vatican City, then we can see the entrance. The obelisk majestically stands at the center of the square.
If we see the obelisk only, we may visit here at any time. However I recommend to climb up to the Cupola of St. Peter's. But we will receive the security inspection, and the people make a long waiting line in the daytime. So, visiting early in the morning is better. Also, visiting Vatican Museums is recommended. The admission ticket for the Museums, and the Sistine Chapel (Cappella Sistina) where there are the "Last Judgment" and the ceiling paintings is a set, and is available on the day. However, it takes more than 2 hours waiting line to obtain it, so purchasing online is recommended.

About The Obelisk:
The Provenance: The provenance of this obelisk is not well clarified.
According to one source, "The Natural History" authored by Pliny the Elder (Plinius) (An ancient Roman natural historian in AD 1st century), Nuncoreus, a son of Pharaoh Sesostris I (or Kheperkare Senusret I) (Pharaoh of Middle Kingdom, 12th Dynasty, reigned in 20th century BC) erected a pair of obelisk (2 obelisks) at the Temple in Heliopolis in token of his thanks for having recovered from blindness. One another obelisk (100 cubits high) still remains. [The Natural History, Volume 36, Chapter 15]
However, The stories in "The Natural History" is often a fake, but contains a lot of interesting fantastic stories. Hence we cannot acknowledge all the contents are fact, and must handle this carefully.
"The Natural History" doesn't refer to the location where the (pair of) obelisks were erected, and "Nuncoreus" doesn't exist in the history.
On the other hand, "Histories" ("historiai") authored by Herodotus (An ancient Greek historian in 5th century BC), King Pheron (Pharaoh Pheros) erected a pair of obelisk (2 obelisks) at the Temple in Heliopolis in token of his thanks for having recovered from blindness. [Histories, Volume 2, Section 111]
Since these stories are quite similar, Pliny the Elder might have copied from Herodotus' "Histories".
Pheros may be a common noun as the spelling of "pharaoh" and "pheros" are similar and this might be a derivative of "pharaoh".
According to another source, "The obelisk was quarried in Aswan in the era of Amenemhet II (Middle Kingdom, 12th Dynasty, 20th century BC), and erected at the Temple of Sun in Heliopolis.

However, the critical questions exist. This obelisk does not have the usual hieroglyph. It's hardly to believe the obelisk without hieroglyph was made in the time of Middle Kingdom, 12th Dynasty, in 20th century BC. It's also hardly to believe that Ramses II (13th century BC) overlooked it, and didn't make it as his own obelisk. Also, the current obelisk in Heliopolis has hieroglyph, but the Pharaoh name is Senusret I (Sesostris I), not Nuncoreus.

In anyway, this obelisk was brought to Alexandria and erected at the Julian Forum in Alexandria by Gaius Cornelius Gallus, the first Roman prefect of Egypt under Octavianus (the first Roman Emperor Augustus [reigned 27 BC - AD 14]), and was taken by Roman Emperor Caligula in AD 37, for Rome, and erected it as a spina of the Caligula Circus, later the Nero Circus (Circus Gai et Neronis, or the Vatican Circus).

In the creation myth of the Heliopolitan form of ancient Egyptian religion, Benben was the mound that arose from the primordial waters (Nu), and upon which the creator deity Atum settled. The Benben stone is associated with the top stone of a pyramid, which is called a pyramid's pyramidion (or benbenet). It is also related to the obelisk.

Primeval mound
In the Pyramid Texts, e.g. Utterances 587 and 600, Atum himself is at times referred to as "mound". It was said to have turned into a small pyramid, located in Heliopolis (Egyptian: Annu or Iunu), within which Atum was said to dwell. Other cities developed their own myths of the primeval mound. At Memphis, the god Tatenen, an earth god and the origin of "all things in the shape of food and viands, divine offers, all good things", was the personification of the primeval mound.

Benben stone
The Benben stone, named after the mound, was a sacred stone in the temple of Ra at Heliopolis (Egyptian: Annu or Iunu). It was the location on which the first rays of the sun fell. It is thought to have been the prototype for later obelisks, and the capstones of the great pyramids were based on its design. The capstone (the tip of the pyramid) is also called a pyramidion. In ancient Egypt, these were probably polished or clad so they shone in sunlight.[citation needed]

Many Benben stones, often carved with images and inscriptions, are found in museums around the world.

The bird deity Bennu, which was probably the inspiration for the phoenix, was venerated at Heliopolis, where it was said to be living on the Benben stone or on the holy willow tree.

According to Barry Kemp, the connection between the benben, the phoenix, and the sun may well have been based on alliteration: the rising, weben, of the sun sending its rays towards the benben, on which the bennu bird lives. Utterance 600, § 1652 of the Pyramid Texts speaks of Atum as you rose up, as the benben, in the Mansion of the Bennu in Heliopolis.[1]

Historical development
From the earliest times, the portrayal of Benben was stylized in two ways; the first was as a pointed, pyramidal form, which was probably the model for pyramids and obelisks. The other form was round-topped; this was probably the origin of Benben as a free standing votive object and an object of veneration.[2]

During the Fifth Dynasty, the portrayal of benben was formalized as a squat obelisk. Later, during the Middle Kingdom, this became a long, thin obelisk.

In the Amarna Period tomb of Panehesy, the benben is seen as a large, round-topped stela standing on a raised platform.[3]

Honored to meet a fellow traveler | Sen. Raphael Warnock had private meeting with the Pope
Georgia’s U.S. senator recalled his visit with the late Jorge Mario Bergolio at The Vatican last year.
By Andy Pierrotti and Tim Darnell
Published: Apr. 21, 2025 at 1:49 AM PDT| Updated: Apr. 21, 2025 at 5:40 AM PDT

ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) - Almost a year ago, U.S. Sen. Raphael Warnock had a private meeting with Pope Francis at The Vatican

“I was deeply honored to meet not only the leader of the Catholic Church, but a fellow traveler,” Warnock said of the late Pontiff, who died Monday, April 21, 2025.

Warnock’s Papal visit was part of an April 2024 trip that involved briefings with the NATO Defense College and the World Food Programme.

Warnock said the two spoke and prayed about humanitarian crises across the globe, including Sudan, Ukraine and Palestinians in Gaza, still in the midst of a deadly conflict between Israel and Hamas. Warnock said Francis, with the help of an interpreter, told him he was in regular contact with a small congregation of Catholics in Gaza.

Jorge Mario Bergolio was born in Argentina Dec, 17, 1936, he was appointed Archbishop of Buenos Aires in 2001 and, taking the name of Pope Francis, was elected Supreme Pontiff on March 13, 2013.

The 88-year-old pope, who has chronic lung disease and had part of one lung removed as a young man, was hospitalized several weeks ago for treatment of pneumonia.

Warnock has led Ebenezer Baptist Church - Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s former pastoral home - since 2005. Francis was elected by a papal conclave in 2013 at the age of 76, leading more than 1.3 billion Catholics across the globe.

Often revered and criticized as one of the most progressive popes in history, Francis had expressed support to address climate change, immigration and the LGBTQ community.

Warnock said the late Pontiff’s position on those issues demonstrated his focus on human decency. “That doesn’t mean we always land on the same side of every issue, but what I see in him is an effort to center human dignity,” Warnock said.

The senator said he and the late Pope shared a few laughs, but “I’ll keep that between us,” he said.

Martin Pradier, our Materials Analyst, joined BNN Bloomberg to discuss the recent gold rally and offer his three Hot Picks in the sector. He said the gold rally will continue but "at a slower pace," noting that interest rates will present a headwind. 

Martin likes Franco-Nevada because of its anticipated reopening of the Cobre Panama mine, a key catalyst. He also likes copper miner HudBay Minerals, noting it has the lowest cost structure, strongest growth and lowest valuation relative to peers. Interestingly, Martin explains why HudBay's cost structure is so low: "They're mining copper, but copper comes with a byproduct, and the product is gold," which covers all the copper mining costs. 

His third pick, Wheaton Precious Metals, has strong growth prospects and a fixed cost structure at a time when gold mining costs have risen 15-20% in recent quarters.

On January 17, 2020, Jim Mullin, the teenage son of U.S. Senator Markwayne Mullin (R-OK), suffered a severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) during a high school wrestling accident. The injury left him unresponsive with an extremely low pulse for 26 hours. When he woke up, he experienced profound cognitive and motor deficits, requiring him to completely relearn how to walk, read, and perform basic functions. [1, 2, 3, 4]

The Extent of the Injury & Rehabilitation

Cognitive Regression: Jim went from operating at a high school academic level to a third-grade learning level practically overnight. He struggled with basic motor functions, short-term memory loss, and simple arithmetic. [1, 2, 3, 4]
Physical Impact: An elite, world-class youth wrestler, he lost muscle control and could no longer touch his nose or walk without shuffling his feet. [1, 2]
[1, 2, 3]Recovery: Jim underwent intensive, specialized rehabilitation at the Center for Neuro Skills in Bakersfield, California. Doctors initially estimated his recovery would take two to three years, but he was discharged to return home after nine months of progress in October 2020.

Connection to Donald Trump

The incident became a major focal point in March 2026 during Markwayne Mullin's Senate confirmation hearing for Secretary of Homeland Security. An emotional Mullin recounted how the tragedy forged his deep, unwavering personal loyalty to Donald Trump: [1, 2, 3]
Personal Outreach: Upon learning of the injury in 2020, Trump immediately called Mullin, offered his personal plane to transport Jim to the California neural rehab facility, and followed up with near-daily phone calls. [1, 2]
The Visit: In the middle of his 2020 reelection campaign, Trump flew to Bakersfield to visit Jim privately without any press or cameras. Mullin noted that Trump spent 15 minutes engaging with Jim, an interaction that significantly boosted the teenager's morale and visibly helped trigger his short-term memory recovery. [1, 2, 3]

text:
The Abandoned Gold Rush Town of Independence Colorado

High in the Colorado Rockies sits the remains of a gold rush town that once attracted hundreds of prospectors searching for fortune.

We traveled to Independence, Colorado, to explore this fascinating historic ghost town and personally recorded our own footage of its surviving buildings, abandoned structures, and beautiful mountain surroundings. In this video, you’ll see the location through our eyes as we walk through the remnants of a town frozen in Colorado’s mining history.

Independence experienced a remarkable rise during the late 1800s. By 1882, it had dozens of businesses, a gold processing mill, and a population estimated at around 1,000 people.

But the gold wouldn’t last.

When the mines closed, residents began abandoning the settlement and heading toward nearby Aspen. Within just a few years, Independence had gone from a thriving mining town to a nearly forgotten mountain settlement.

Then came the winter of 1899.

With heavy snowfall blocking mountain routes and food supplies running dangerously low, the handful of residents still living in Independence faced a desperate decision.

Their solution? They reportedly built approximately 75 pairs of homemade wooden skis and prepared to escape through the snow toward Aspen.

And in an almost unbelievable twist, their departure reportedly turned into a ski race.

Today, the surviving historic buildings offer a glimpse into Colorado’s mining past and the extraordinary story of a town that rose quickly, lost its fortune, and was eventually left behind.

Join us at @WorldsRewound as we explore Independence, Colorado, combining our own footage from visiting this historic ghost town with its fascinating history.

📍 LOCATION: Independence, Colorado, USA

If you enjoy exploring abandoned towns, forgotten history, ghost towns, lost civilizations, and fascinating places around the world, make sure to:

👍 LIKE this video if you enjoyed the journey.

🔔 Follow @WorldsRewound​⁠  for more real world explorations, abandoned places, and incredible stories from history.

text:
5 Years of Struggle & Spreading Hope

The Center for Political Innovation Activities 2021-2026

https://t.co/XROvWXdqCW

By Caleb Maupin, Founder & Director

The Center for Political Innovation has existed for five years now, and in that time it has far exceeded my expectations. I always intended for the group to be an organization of action, bringing people into the struggle against globalism/imperialism, functioning as a network of activists.

The first in-person gathering was in June 2021 in Saxton, Pennsylvania. We gathered for three days in a rented hunting lodge. The gathering included 42 people in total, from different regions of the United States and different backgrounds. I gave a series of interactive classes we have called “The Saxton Lectures,” laying out an organizational vision and perspective.

Nicaragua Solidarity & Exposing BreadTube

At the time we called ourselves “The City-Building Tendency” and viewed our movement as a form of anti-revisionist Communism. There were many people who joined the group with competing visions.

After the Saxton Lectures we threw ourselves into Nicaragua solidarity, supporting this socialist country in Central America. We defended the foreign minister of Nicaragua when he spoke at church in Manhattan that was besieged by anti-government exiles. We also sent a three-person delegation to Nicaragua to monitor the elections, for which we were highlighted in Business weekly.

While in Nicaragua, I got to have a conversation with the son of President Daniel Ortega, Laureano Ortega, about economics and the way imperialism was breaking down. The Sandinistas really valued our support and publicizing their election giving a popular mandate to their Christian Socialist anti-imperialist government that has lifted millions from poverty.

During these early months, I exposed BreadTube, a network of popular YouTube channels and social media influencers speaking in the name of socialism while preaching hatred for Russia and waging cancel culture hate campaigns against anti-imperialist voices. My book was called BreadTube Serves Imperialism. https://t.co/VbfxXuLWxy

I revealed that a known US intelligence operative was advising them and that they were most likely a psychological operation to confuse young people inspired by Bernie Sanders. While my work was initially mocked, it has now been confirmed we were far more correct than we knew. Max Blumenthal revealed that one of the top BreadTube personalities was on the payroll of British intelligence. Since then, ties to Hillary Clinton have also been revealed.

Clashing with the Communist Party

The Communist Party USA became desperate and vicious in response to us. Entire meetings of the National Committee were devoted to the “threat” of CPI. We never wanted hostility toward the Communist Party and many of our early members were registered in both organizations.

Many times, I called the Communist Party’s office offering to talk with the leaders and come to some kind of understanding. Many times my personal cell phone number was given to CPUSA chairman Joe Simms by party members who wanted the unnecessary tension to be resolved. The Communist Party refused to communicate, but instead ultimately published a deranged smear piece which remains on their website to this day.  https://t.co/IND28ffSXx

The piece quotes our textbook “We are City Builders,” https://t.co/YXCdzkrIFd  which honors the Black Panthers and hails the heroic anti-racist work of their organization, claiming it is somehow a “white supremacist” book. The article claims we are “fascist” because we call for a “Government of Action” which is similar to phrases used by Oswald Mosley, and because we honor Louisiana Governor Huey Long, a beloved populist of the 1930s for whom Black Panther leader Huey Newton was named. The real reason they think we are “fascist,” of course, is because we did not march behind Joe Biden and his anti-Russia hysteria.

At the time the Communist Party USA was panicking about CPI, State Department employees were regularly stopping in at their 23rd Street, New York City headquarters, urging them to be more anti-Russian. A woman with a mysterious history of wrecking organizations and burning bridges, who had presided over the collapse of Workers World Party in 2017, was suddenly leading the Young Communist League and making sure they barely functioned, all while obsessively talking about the Center for Political Innovation and why it must be stopped at every meeting.

The smear piece on the Communist Party website is a badge of honor. David Rovics’s song mocking US Communist groups says “The CP will just do their thing / And pretend the others don't exist” referring to how the Communist Party generally considers itself above polemics against rival organizations, considering itself to be in a different league. Well, the CPUSA may not be threatened by some Trotskyite sect or a teenage Anarchist club, but they certainly are threatened by the Center for Political Innovation, despite the fact that we always sought to be on good terms with them. While we meant no hostility, the truth is that our anti-imperialist work, carried out while educating people about the best moments in their own history exposes their current existence as a Democratic Party volunteer squad for the betrayal it truly is.

The fact that we maintained a street presence, having rallies in Central Park, doing regular canvassing and outreach in different regions of the country, in addition to the constant online livestreaming made us even more threatening.

“Russia is not our enemy!”

Right after Russia’s special military operation was launched, our rallying cry was “Russia is not our enemy!” We marched in the streets and convened a successful conference in Austin, Texas themed around solidarity with the people of the Donbass against the NATO regime. Our conference made a big splash.

At the time, certain social media influencers who appear to have been coordinating with the FBI approached us, appearing friendly. They then began recruiting people inside the organization to function as agents for a major attempt to destroy our organization that failed.

We continued holding “Russia is not our enemy” rallies around the country, and held a national training school in Linn Valley, Kansas. We then proceeded to build a major anti-imperialist conference in Chicago. Just a week before the conference, the FBI raided the homes of the Uhuru Movement activists in St. Louis, Missouri, and St. Petersburg, Florida. We immediately called them offering full solidarity and support, and welcomed them as heroes to our August 2022 convention in Chicago. We also honored Tara Reade for her work as a journalist in the face of a huge amount of state repression from the Democratic Party.

Prior to the convention, I was blackmailed. An ex-member who had been recruited and was consulting with and working alongside the social media influencers spoke to me on the phone and said, “you’re going to have to cancel the conference.” Other speakers at the conference received similar mysterious messages. The FBI clearly did not appreciate that we were about to publicize and call out their attack on a group of Black anti-imperialists. One of the members who had been recruited to act as an informant insisted we shouldn’t oppose the raids on Black activists who had been labelled “a cult.”

Despite all the pressure I was placed under, we decided we would proceed with the conference. It was a smashing success. The Uhuru Movement was welcomed as heroes. Tara Reade gave a stirring anti-imperialist speech. Garland Nixon and other allies found the day’s events to be inspiring and exhilarating. Nick Brana of the Peoples Party left the event inspired to organize some kind of anti-war rally in Washington, DC.

As retaliation for this anti-imperialist conference and for supporting the Uhuru movement and calling out the FBI, vicious personal attacks were unloaded against me and CPI on the internet. The accusations were baseless. A lot of innuendo, reinterpretation of events, and outright lies. Meanwhile, people in the group who had been recruited by these social media personalities proceeded to try and destroy our organizational assets. There was a struggle to keep control of the website, bank accounts, Twitter and YouTube accounts, etc.

This is the manner in which the Cult Awareness Network, coordinating with US intelligence and/or the FBI normally targets organizations. Members are recruited and planted as “sleepers,” mainstream media is coordinated with, the attack comes all at once with disinformation everywhere. This is how Gerry Healy’s Workers Revolutionary Party was crushed as far back as 1985. The Democratic Workers Party led by Marlene Dixon was targeted in a similar manner. Various religious and political groups that have become the target of the deep state have undergone similar operations.

The deep state assumed that because we had not been functioning as an organization for very long, we would immediately buckle and surrender. They were wrong. We did shed a number of people who did not have the stamina for such attacks and were not really loyal to the project. Because we still categorized ourselves as a “communist” group we had a number of people who had no real loyalty to our principles and teachings and just wanted to identify with the hammer and sickle. Such people are not very useful in building a real organization. If they can’t stand internet sex gossip and smearing, how can they pretend they will be Che Guevara when the moment arrives? It’s unfortunate how for many young people political activism is just a kind of internet fantasy. For CPI, it never has been this. We intend to rescue our country from the nightmare of imperialist/globalist decay and build an anti-monopoly coalition.

Back at the Center of the Action

We re-emerged publicly 3 months after the attack. Almost immediately, we were once again at the center of attention as official sponsors of the Rage Against the War Machine protests in Washington, DC. Nick Brana and Angela McArdle of the Libertarian Party had been inspired to call the rally and our logo was featured on all the protest posters and communications. When Scott Ritter was forced to step out of the rally, we rented a hotel in downtown DC and organized an “after party” where he was welcomed to a thunderous crowd chanting “Scott! Scott! Scott!” Our after-party was attended by over 200 people from around the country, including Noah Schenck whose life circumstances had finally permitted him to become fully involved.

We followed the successful Washington, DC demonstration with a gathering called the “Summit Against Hypocrisy” to counter Biden’s ‘Summit for Democracy.’ This three-day anti-imperialist conference was yet another smashing success. Not only did we gather anti-imperialist voices, protest at the White House and allow anti-imperialists to network, but we then confronted Tsai Ing-wen on the streets of New York City just days afterward saying “Stop Selling War in Our Country! We don’t want a new war against China! China is not our enemy!” https://t.co/1lRHdxaDM8

In September of that year, I had the honor of conducting a face-to-face sit-down interview with Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi when he was at the United Nations. The interview was only possible because of my job as an RT reporter, but also my years of visiting Iran and speaking up against Israeli crimes. The fact that I was trusted by the Iranian head of state and his team for a sit-down conversation, something heads of state are especially careful about granting with American journalists, testifies to how much our organization is valued by anti-imperialist forces across the planet.

In February 2024, the Center for Political Innovation led the US delegation to the World Youth Festival in Sochi, Russia. We held a press conference at the United Nations raising the Uhuru case and talking about US threats against those who visited Russia and told the truth about the Ukraine conflict. At the World Youth Festival, Noah and I were invited to a special session where we got to directly speak to the Russian President, and speak for the American majority that is tired of the wars and wants a better relationship with the world.

The Streamer Raid & Khrushchev-ist Fight

When I returned from Russia, we were able to hold a training workshop in Vermont, but almost immediately we faced yet another organizational conflict. In reality we were hit with two major attacks at once. The first came from outside forces, the same social media influencers who had pretended to be friendly to us while coordinating the major attack in 2022. They formed a new “party” and with advertising from CNN and other mainstream media outlets, insisted they were the new vanguard of the American working class. We contacted them and they told us they wanted no relationship with CPI, however, they called up our members around the country and urged them to quit CPI.

We lost a few people, but not very many. Those we lost were mostly chronically online people who had never really plugged into the actual activism of the group. This “party” formed by social media influencers is nothing more than a social media fan club. Members of the group have had the FBI come to their homes, and rather than speaking up to support them, the “party” just expels or disavows them. Despite claiming to support Russia and having people from millionaire families in leadership positions, this “organization” did nothing to support the Uhuru movement in light of the FBI’s efforts to to criminalize pro-Russia speech.

At the same time as we had to deal with the streamer raid, two people in the leadership of CPI had a Khrushchev-ist meltdown. Unlike the streamers and wreckers, these people most likely had good intentions and suffered from some genuinely hard personal circumstances. However, they were determined to prove to family members or romantic partners that CPI conformed to liberal standards, something no genuine anti-imperialist organization will ever do. They held pessimistic feelings about organizational growth, and continued to try and invent procedures or bureaucratic structures where they could prevent activism from taking place in order to prove to themselves we were “democratic.”

It’s quite interesting because CPI remains pretty loose in terms of regulating members. Our membership contains people with a variety of different perspectives on social issues who support our overall mission. We permit people to speak for themselves on social media and create their own writings and content if they desire.

However, it wasn’t enough simply to have freedom for members, the Khrushchev-ists wanted structures to prevent the organization from taking action. They were desperate to create some kind of mechanism through which they could silence or suppress me, the founder and director, in order to prove the organization was not a “cult of personality” as their hostile, pro-imperialist relatives and romantic partners insisted. It was an absurd demand to make, and could never be clearly articulated. They were both asked if there were certain reforms they wanted in order to remain involved, and they couldn’t specify any. All they could offer was gloomy hopelessness about the future of the organization, and liberal platitudes about “cult of personality.”

The Khrushchev-ists may have had good intentions, but despite being only two people, they managed to do significant damage when they departed, wrecking the dues collection system among other things. Now new active members study the book Khruschevism: A Study in Psychological Warfare as part of their training. https://t.co/d0UGbeI8A6

Surging Forward in the 2024 Election

After they departed, simultaneously with the streamer raid, CPI surged ahead once again. The book I had written on Kamala Harris, Kamala Harris and the Future of America, was banned from Amazon on the very day she became the presumptive nominee of the Democrats in the 2024 election. With CPI being featured on many major YouTube channels, and Amazon backing down and restoring the book seven days later, we suddenly had lots of funds coming in from book revenue and lots of new members signing up. https://t.co/8KfIlq0XsQ

We dispatched a team of volunteers to the Democratic National Convention in Chicago where we distributed 1,000 copies of the Kamala Harris book to crowds outside the convention. We then launched our “PeaceMAGA” operation, bringing a huge banner of Trump and Kim Jong Un shaking hands to the streets of Manhattan, with the words “Only Peace Can Make America Great Again.” Our PeaceMAGA campaign made a huge splash, featured various media outlets such as the New Yorker and USA Today. We took the banner to the inauguration as well and distributed thousands of anti-imperialist booklets to those attending Trump’s swearing-in ceremony in the freezing streets of DC. https://t.co/PnYJvW9btr

We did not endorse Trump, as we do not endorse any political candidates and do not support political campaigns or electioneering of any kind. Most of our members did not vote for Trump, though a few may have. We made the strategic decision to boost the anti-war messaging in his 2024 campaign and emphasize that this is what the American people wanted from their president. This message created the political space for many within MAGA to break with the White House for betraying these promises.

Some have criticized the PeaceMAGA campaign, but the fruits of our work are everywhere to be seen. When Trump launched his illegal war on Iran, betraying his campaign promises, a big chunk of his supporters broke with him. Joe Kent, his counterterrorism director stepped down. Tucker Carlson, Thomas Massie and Marjorie Taylor Greene spoke up loudly against him.

The Innovationist Turn

Around this time we decided to break with “Communism” as a political identity, because we have transcended to a higher stage. We are anti-imperialists and we advocate a society where profits are no longer in command and the economy is organized to serve the public good, but we do not believe in the destructive philosophy of dialectical materialism. Innovationism is a higher stage of thinking to which we have ascended. Our focus is on celebrating human creativity and enabling people to find their voice, and building a community of resistance where people can be embraced as they join the struggle. This is not what “Communism” means to most people, and it’s not what “communist” groups are doing.

Furthermore, begging for a place within the train wreck that calls itself “communism” in America, trying to own or compete within a dead, tainted brand of politics, is not productive. Communism in the 20th century had big victories against imperialism, and we uphold and celebrate what was achieved. However, the rising new economies around the world no longer espouse the dialectical perspective but emphasize unity and community. The rising new economy in the east embraces markets as part of their overall pro-growth economy, led by a popular state rooted in anti-colonial struggles. Calling ourselves “communist” doesn’t communicate who we are effectively or show what we are trying to do, and it doesn’t help people understand what we are trying to communicate about the world.

We are proud to call ourselves Innovationists, building on the foundations of all our work, and all the heroic anti-imperialist struggles that have come before.

A Consistent Voice of Anti-Imperialism

In 2025 we launched massive distributions of our book Who Are the Houthis? What Are They Fighting For? https://t.co/llbUfr7bBl  The book has been well received by different layers of US society. Iranian-Americans have been so moved by the book that it has been translated into Farsi and is being widely studied across Iran.

In 2025, we held our national convention honoring Angela McArdle for her anti-war work and supporting the Uhuru movement. We also began holding rallies honoring Ibrahim Traoré, the leader of Burkina Faso as an anti-imperialist icon and example of the kind of revolutionary leader the world desperately needs. These rallies have been very well received by Americans and international audiences alike. Our member Penny Arcos has written two books going into depth about Traore’s achievements as an example of a “government of action.”  Her first book is Africa’s Flame: The Rise of Ibrahim Troare. https://t.co/JWu5Fcnggz

Her newer book The AES Effect: How the Alliance of Sahel States is building a New World. https://t.co/rXfnYnAx1R

When Maduro was kidnapped, we swung into action. Not only were we in the streets that same day, but we brought a delegation of activists to the very gates of the jail where he is being held, saying “Free Maduro Now!”

We have defined ourselves as outspoken anti-war voices, being featured on prominent YouTube channels in Los Angeles and blocking the “No Kings” parade in New York City waving Iranian flags and placards calling out the Democrats and advocating solidarity with the Islamic Republic against Zionist war.

We have begun distributing a booklet about anti-imperialism featuring the flower Kimilsungia called “Why is it impossible to get this flower in America?” https://t.co/idC7gCqZ1C  The book has been handed to hundreds of college students and others as a way of starting a conversation about the struggle against imperialism and the achievements of socialism in People’s Korea. We held 14 sessions of the Juche Study Group.

Marching Ahead

Our Los Angeles team is frequently in the streets as is our Minneapolis team, and the New York City local group has begun functioning more regularly with forums and protests in Manhattan.

During our national convention and 7-day program in Chicago this summer we protested the Obama library saying “Obama Killed Gaddafi! Long Live Gaddafi!”  We also said “France out of Africa!” with a spirited rally supporting Ibrahim Traoré at the French consulate.

We have a workshop in Los Angeles scheduled for November 21, register here: https://t.co/mrVN2LUgNz

We have a book release event in New York City set for December 16, register here:  https://t.co/EOOfIEODHX

We are in the streets, reaching new people, challenging the lies of the war-makers, and promoting the need for a government of action that fights for working families. We ask those who appreciate our efforts to donate so we can sustain our work in this period where costs are high and funds can often be tight. https://t.co/nzFsz5hBiF

Each operation we carry out and each internal battle have led us to sharpen our abilities more sharply. BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Wednesday, November 9, 1960, Braniff International Airways inaugurated service between San Antonio, Texas and Mexico City, Mexico. The new nonstop service marked the first time that Braniff had offered flights between the United States Mainland and our friends directly to the south.

In 1945, Aerovias Braniff, an airline owned by Braniff Airways cofounder Thomas Elmer Braniff, operated within Mexico but the service was discontinued after flying just over one year because the Mexican Government revoked the carrier's operating certificates. The revocation was caused by pressure from rival Pan American World Airways that resulted in nearly 15 years of legal battles between the Mexican Government and Braniff. Mr. Braniff had hoped to build his Mexico airline and then obtain Civil Aeronautics Board approval to merge it with Braniff Airways, Incorporated. However, the revocation of Aerovias' operating certificates dashed any hopes of creating a Mexico division.

Braniff Airways had received Civil Aeronautics Board authority to serve Mexico City and Monterrey, Mexico, on May 22, 1946. This was authorized at the same time the carrier was awarded its 7719-mile route system into Cuba and Central and South America. The legal wrangling between Braniff Airways and the Mexican Government, stemming from the Aerovias Braniff incident had been a barrier to service prior to November 1960. Finally, after 15 years Braniff Airways received authority from the Mexican Government to operate to Mexico.

Braniff's new service added 728 unduplicated route miles to its Central and South American route system and provided convenient service from the Heartland of America to the Mexican capitol city. Single-plane service was available from Kansas City and Minneapolis/St Paul as well as the first single-carrier service to Mexico from many cities in the Midwest. Braniff revised its system schedules to coordinate with the new service, which afforded connections from 17 cities across 11 states.

Luxurious new 69-passenger Lockheed L-188 Electra four-engine turboprop aircraft were operated over the new route that flew nonstop to Mexico City from San Antonio International Airport. Braniff had begun taking delivery of its first Electras in the spring of 1959, which were perfectly suited for the medium-range routes with lower passenger loads. Braniff Jet-Powered Electras were fitted with 15 First Class and 54 Coach seats, which offered ample legroom and comfort in both seat types.

Braniff's southbound flight of the day departed Minneapolis/St Paul mid-morning and continued to Kansas City, Dallas Love Field, San Antonio and then arrived in Mexico City late in the afternoon. The flight was perfectly scheduled for arriving in time for dinner at a Mexico City hotspot. The northbound flight to Minneapolis departed early afternoon and made intermediate stops at San Antonio, Dallas, and Kansas City before proceeding to Minneapolis where it arrived late evening just in time for after dinner drinks.

On the afternoon of November 9, 1960, Braniff's first southbound flight to Mexico City departed at 10AM from Minneapolis/St Paul with local dignitaries on board. Braniff Board Chairman Fred Jones, President Charles Edmund Beard, Executive Vice President J. W. "Bill" Miller and Vice President of Public Relations Walter Mark Henshel and Senior Vice President Reginald K. “Rex" Brack (Saleswere hosts on the inaugural flight. Brief ceremonies were held at Minneapolis and Kansas City where additional guests boarded the festive flight.

Dignitaries included Chambers of Commerce presidents, mayors, government officials and media publishers who represented each of the cities served along the route between Minneapolis/St Paul and Mexico City. At Dallas, the group was greeted by Dallas Mayor Pro Tem Elgin B. Robertson and Dallas Morning News City Editor John E. King and were given a jumbo-sized postcard with a special greeting to the People of Mexico.

President Beard, Mayor Pro Tem Robertson, and City Editor King posed for the news media in front of the big Jet-Powered Electra with the giant postcard. Additional guests boarded and the four massive 13 foot 6 inch Aeroproducts propellers began turning at the urging of the equally massive 3750 shaft-horsepower Allison 501-D13 turboprop engines that quickly roared to life. The big airliner taxied and then departed for San Antonio where it landed an hour later.

Additional ceremonies were held at the San Antonio Airport where representatives from that city boarded the Electra for the nonstop leg to Mexico City. The flight departed at 415PM and after a memorable dinner aboard the plane it arrived in Mexico City to a huge red carpet welcome. The guests stayed in Mexico City for five days and an amazing schedule of events had been planned that was enjoyed by all.

Braniff Vice President of Public Relations Walter M. Henshel, in a note to the inaugural passengers, warned them not to drink water or eat fresh fruits and vegetables from out-of-the-way places. He noted that food and beverages from major hotels were more than satisfactory. The note also stated that a special tap with safe drinking water was available over each bathtub in their hotel rooms.

A special Braniff Handicap Race was held at the Hipodromo de las Americas race track that included the attendance of Braniff Hostesses Gloria Brown and Pat Henderson, Mexico City Manager Lee Gonzalez and President Beard who were all at the finish line to congratulate the winner. Jockey Armando Mejio guided his 5-year old mare Heavenly Bliss to a picture perfect win.

The American Chamber of Commerce held a wonderful luncheon for the group at The University Club. The highlight of the visit was the invitation from Mexico President Adolfo Lopez Mateos to visit him at his private residence, Los Pinos. President Mateos posed for photos with the city and Braniff leaders during the visit. Braniff's southbound inaugural guests returned to the United States on November 13, but if they wanted to stay longer arrangements had been made allowing their return tickets to remain valid until November 29.

On November 15, another group returned with the southbound guests on the northbound Electra Flight that departed at 1250PM. The northbound guests included a contingent of 12 Mexican officials that flew to meet their American counterparts in each of the cities where the flight stopped along the route. San Antonio Mayor J. Edwin Kuykendall, who had flown to Mexico City on the November 9, inaugural flight, met with Mexico's Chief Justice of the Supreme Court Alfonso Guzman Neyra, while there. The Chief Justice accompanied the Mexican guests during their tour of the Central United States.

The group enjoyed a four-day roundtrip flight that took them to San Antonio, Dallas, Kansas City and Minneapolis/St Paul. Overnight stays and welcoming ceremonies were enjoyed first at Kansas City then Minneapolis on Wednesday night, and finally Dallas, on Friday evening before heading back to Mexico City, on Saturday, November 19. The group was met by Braniff President Beard upon arrival at Love Field and were taken on a tour of Braniff's Operations and Maintenance Base and then treated to a lavish dinner that evening at the City Club.

The following morning the group headed to San Antonio where they were treated to a wonderful luncheon at the Petroleum Center Club before boarding their awaiting Electra for the 415PM flight back home. Guests that wanted to remain in the United States for an additional amount of time were told that their tickets were good for 30 days.

MVP Stories - Dick Groat 1960 Part V

A trade involving the 1960 MVPs Groat and Maris? It almost happened in ‘59

One week before Dick Groat won the 1960 NL MVP Award, the New York Yankees’ Roger Maris was named the American League’s Most Valuable Player. 

Maris was acquired by the Yankees in December of 1959 in a trade with the Kansas City Athletics. 

Interestingly at the time the Pirates too were seeking to add power to their line-up. 

According to the Pittsburgh Press, Pirates GM Joe Brown, “was working up a package deal with either the (Washington) Senators or A’s – seeking power ….”

Shortly after the Yankees acquired Maris Yankees General Manager, George Weiss, stated that the Yankees “almost didn’t make the deal with the A’s for Maris. A certain National League team (presumably the Pirates) offered three regulars for Maris etc., and Arnold Johnson of Kansas City was ready to accept it.”

Again, according to the Pittsburgh Press, the three players offered by the Pirates were Dick Groat, outfielder Bill Virdon and pitcher Ron Kline. 

One year later Bucs’ GM, Joe Brown, somewhat corroborated the report. According to the Associated Press the talks between the Pirates and the A’s “involved Pittsburgh’s shortstop Dick Groat for slugger Roger Maris…”

“In fact, after one of the sessions, Brown and Manager Danny Murtaugh seemed almost ready to wrap up the deal. They returned to their hotel room in Miami Beach to talk it over.”

“’But as soon as Danny and I closed the door, we looked at each other and frowned – right away we knew we didn’t like it,’ Brown recalled. ‘And the more we thought about it, the less we liked it,’” thus the deal was called off.

text:
Crude Oil Prices Are Falling As Refineries Struggle To Process Supply, Masking a Much Bigger Crisis in Refined Petroleum Products

Oil prices are falling, and market expectations for future inflation are declining alongside them. On the surface, that appears encouraging. But a much larger problem remains beneath the headline numbers.

The global economy does not run on crude oil alone. It runs on refined petroleum products, particularly diesel, gasoline, heating oil and jet fuel. And those markets remain under extraordinary pressure.

What The Bond Market Is Signaling

Goldman Sachs data shows 5 year inflation breakevens falling from approximately 2.75% earlier this year toward 2.3%, with longer maturity measures also declining.

These readings reflect inflation compensation influenced by expectations, risk premiums and market liquidity.

Their decline could reflect improving energy supplies, restrictive monetary policy or weakening economic demand.

But falling inflation expectations do not mean households and businesses are experiencing lower costs.

The Refining Bottleneck

On November 6, Brent crude traded near $98 per barrel. Yet wholesale diesel in New York Harbor was approximately $4.47 per gallon, equivalent to nearly $188 per barrel. Heating oil was approximately $4.25 per gallon.

That represents an extraordinary premium of roughly $90 per barrel for diesel relative to Brent.

According to the Kansas City Fed, refining spreads recently accounted for more than 40% of retail diesel costs, compared with less than 20% historically.

Russian refinery disruptions, Middle Eastern conflict, damaged infrastructure and constrained shipping have reduced global refining throughput.

Meanwhile, American refineries operated above 95% utilization during much of the summer, leaving limited spare capacity.

Even if crude becomes more available, damaged refineries cannot immediately resume production.

Crude prices can therefore decline while finished fuels remain exceptionally expensive.

The Inflation And Demand Destruction Problem

Gasoline directly affects consumer inflation. Diesel has broader implications through freight transportation, agriculture, construction and industrial production.

When diesel remains expensive, transporting food, manufactured goods and raw materials becomes more costly.

Businesses must either pass those costs onto consumers or absorb them through shrinking profit margins.

But with borrowing costs elevated, credit demand weakening and financially constrained households already struggling, passing along additional costs becomes increasingly difficult.

Businesses may respond by reducing investment, operating expenses, employee hours and eventually employment.

Meanwhile, households spending more on fuel, heating and necessities have less income available for everything else.

Even if inflation slows, purchasing power does not automatically recover.

If diesel rises from $4 to $6 per gallon and remains there for another year, annual diesel inflation eventually falls to zero, even though consumers are still paying 50% more.

Lower inflation does not necessarily mean lower prices.

What Markets May Be Missing

The bond market appears to be pricing economic damage from the energy shock rather than its resolution.

Refinery disruptions are reducing crude demand while keeping diesel, heating oil and other finished fuels expensive. Meanwhile, restrictive rates and elevated energy costs are squeezing household spending and corporate margins.

Falling inflation expectations increasingly reflect the prospect of weaker demand, even as fuel shortages persist. Until refining spreads narrow, inventories rebuild and transportation costs fall, cheaper crude offers limited relief.

The economy is absorbing an unresolved energy shock through demand destruction, not restored supply.

That is not healthy disinflation. It is economic deterioration.

text:
Richard Feynman lied to a librarian to borrow a calculus book. He was only about 13 years old.

In the early 1930s, trigonometry was the highest mathematics course offered at Far Rockaway High School in New York. But Feynman wanted to learn calculus, so he turned to a book by J. E. Thompson called Calculus for the Practical Man.

When he tried to borrow it, the librarian questioned why a child wanted such a book. Feynman told her it was for his father.

He took it home and taught himself calculus.

What makes this story remarkable is that his original notebook still exists.

Preserved at the Niels Bohr Library & Archives, the small green notebook contains handwritten explanations, carefully copied diagrams, formulas, and an index he created himself. His notes cover the entire book.

There was also a moment he never forgot.

When his father tried reading the book, he struggled to understand the opening material. Feynman later recalled:

"It was the first time I realized that I could understand what he couldn't understand."

That teenager went on to study at MIT, pursue graduate research at Princeton, work on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos, and share the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physics for his contributions to quantum electrodynamics.

He also developed his own mathematical notation while young, experimenting with different ways of expressing familiar functions.

Decades later, his lectures and diagrams would help generations of physicists understand difficult ideas.

The book in this photograph is the 1946 second edition. Feynman learned from an earlier edition published in the 1930s.

His surviving notebook is a remarkable reminder of what independent study can look like. He didn't simply collect formulas. He worked through the mathematics carefully enough to make it his own.

🔒 Cybersecurity — 🕒 24h Recap

🚨 Attacks & Breaches
- Iris Plaza says a compromised external cloud service may have exposed 7.7 million customers’ personal information. Its shopping platform remains offline during investigation and remediation.
- Frontline Education raised its August breach’s impact to 3,085,266 people, more than twice earlier disclosed totals. Attackers exploited third-party software to steal school employees’ and students’ personal information.
- Sega Sammy’s ($6460.T) gaming unit disclosed 2.2 million newsletter addresses exposed through provider ARARA. Its separate game-account distribution system was unaffected.
- Revolve ($RVLV) told regulators its breach affected 1,515,073 people. The intruder may have collected saved payment-card numbers and expiration dates, along with names and contact information.

🦠 Ransomware & Malware
- Beget says a wiper attack destroyed its cloud data and VPS binary backups, forcing a rebuild from scratch. Only some VPS file backups survived.

🩹 Vulnerabilities & Exploits
- N-able ($NABL) took hosted N-central offline and urged on-premises customers to shut servers after publication of 30-plus alleged zero-days. The company found no evidence of active exploitation or unauthorized data access.
- Attackers are exploiting SSHole to breach certain musl-based Linux systems through OpenSSH authentication bypass. OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes the flaw, with disabling password authentication offered as a mitigation.
- QNAP warns Plex2Shell is being exploited against Plex Media Server on its NAS devices and urges updates to version 1.43.3 or later. The NAS operating systems themselves are unaffected.

🔗 Application & Supply Chain Security
- Mittwald says an attacker exploited its MCP server to compromise 56 customer projects after eight days undetected. The company suspects AI assistance, but supplied no evidence distinguishing it from conventional scripts.

🏭 Critical Infrastructure & OT
- France blamed an IRGC-linked unit for October’s refrigeration sabotage at roughly 700 French retail sites and pursued EU sanctions. Its attribution does not cover November’s European or blood-bank incidents.

🔐 Data Protection & Cryptography
- Google DeepMind, part of Alphabet ($GOOGL), says supervised AI agents cut RSA-1024 signature-forgery CPU cost 3.5-fold. The result concerns obsolete keys, with modern 2048-bit-or-larger encryption remaining secure.

🛡️ Detection, Response & Defense
- The White House nominated Palantir ($PLTR) security chief Michael LoSapio to lead CISA, which has lacked a Senate-confirmed director for almost 22 months.

Curiously, terror tactics often involve mutilating the third eye (the seat of insight and secret thoughts) and playing on fears of an "all-seeing" cosmic eye of God. To appreciate the "sobering effects" of the "malevolent" and "mysterious" eye of God, it helps to know something of the archetype's mythological origins. In ancient Egypt, the eye of God was plucked from Horus, an anthropomorphic sun-god with a falcon's head. Pictured as the morning sun cresting a pyramid, the eye of God represents the dawn of self-awareness, when the ego emerged from the id and no longer required human sacrifice to overcome its primeval anxiety. Awed by the falcon's superlative sight, talons, and flight, the Egyptians endowed Horus with the bird's predatory prowess, so he could avenge the murder his father, Osiris, whose name means "seat of the eye." Set on high, scanning the earth for the forces of darkness, the falcon as sun-god -- as the manifestation of enlightenment -- carries out the work of organization and pacification, imposing moral order on earth.
The eye of God assumes its mysterious "counterespionage" qualities through this myth of the eternal cycle -- the battle between good and evil -- in which, if the perfidious gods of darkness can guess the sun-god's secret name, they can rob him of his powers and trap him forever in the underworld. Thus a falcon emblem was placed above the gates of all Egyptian temples, scanning for the sun-god's enemies, while the sun-god relied on code names to conceal his identity.
Oddly enough, the eye of God was the symbol of the Cao Dai sect, whose gallery of saints include Confucius, Buddha, Joan of Arc, Jesus, and Victor Hugo. Inside the Cao Dai cathedral in Tay Ninh City, the Cao Dai pope divined upon his planchette the secrets of the Great pyramid; over the temple door loomed a huge blue "all-seeing" eye surrounded by snakes and trees.
